div.head: II Eg 4
div.ab: ⁊ sy ælc heorðpæning agyfen be Petres mæssedæg.
⁊ sy ælc heorþpening agyfen be Petres mæssedæg.
⁊ sy ælc heorðpænig agifen be Petres mæssedæg.
Et omnis heorðpeni reddatur ad festum sancti Petri.
[Be þon heorþpeninge.] ⁊ sy ælc heorðpænig agifen be Petres mæssedæg.
And sy ælc heorðpæning agyfen be Petres mæssedæg.
(Von dem Herdpfennig. Ld) Und jeder Herdpfennig werde zu Petri Festtag [1. August] abgeliefert.
(Of the hearth-penny. Ld) And let every hearth-penny be paid by St Peter's day [1 August].
And every hearth-penny shall be paid by St Peter’s Day.
And every hearth-penny is to be paid by St Peter’s day.
And every hearth penny is to be paid by the Feast of Saint Peter.

note.label: contrast
note.quote: The thought of a recalcitrant solemnly setting off for Rome ... (2.) is difficult to take seriously. It is no surprise that Wulfstan envisaged something more sensible

heorðpennig (cf. Wulfstan, pp. 116, 208) seems identical with Romfeoh, i.e. Peter’s Pence (cf. I Cn. 9; Wulfstan, pp. 272, 311), which was a tax of a penny levied on every household.

note.label: hearth-penny
note.seg: A penny from every house, by this time identical with Peter’s Pence.

note.label: day
note.seg: Probably the feast of St Peter and St Paul, 29 June; see p. 444, n. 4.
